main_new_result: For the first strong-majority chain block C, full extensions partition exactly into a uniform C-first channel plus first-interruption channels indexed by q in M and interruption depth j. Each channel tail is a genuine uniform linear extension of a strictly smaller residual poset R_{q,j}. Width <=3 forces 1<=|M|<=2. In the one-interrupter case the partner endpoint cap gives 2/3<alpha<7/9 and a protected central interval for Q-pair probabilities; in the two-interrupter case the uniform Q majority direction between the two interrupters cannot reverse and the second interrupter must lie below at least one endpoint Hasse blocker.
exact_recurrence: e(P)=e(Q)+sum_{q in M} sum_{j=lambda(q)}^{m-1} e(R_{q,j}); pair/event probabilities obey the corresponding exact convex mixture of uniform residual-poset laws.
local_transfer_counterexample: A width-three one-interrupter poset with e(Q)=18,e(P)=26, only chain-Q incomparable pair having probability 9/13>2/3, yet a Q-balanced pair 2/3 projects to 9/13. The same P has a 1/2 pair, so POS3 itself is not refuted.
